power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

stat_p_exact.summary_text: We found 2 imprecise *p* values out of 9 detected *p* values.

table.formatted: Cell pairs whose contact decreased with age in controls also tended to be less in contact in DKD than in controls, and pairs whose contact increased with age tended to be more in contact (ρ = 0.65 across the 66 cell pairs; 80.3% of pairs in the same direction; permutation P = 0.0066; Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_2">3a</ref>).
table.header: Spatial and expression changes in DKD
table.expanded: Cell pairs whose contact decreased with age in controls also tended to be less in contact in DKD than in controls, and pairs whose contact increased with age tended to be more in contact (ρ = 0.65 across the 66 cell pairs; 80.3% of pairs in the same direction; permutation P = 0.0066; Figure 3a).

table.formatted: Within DKD, biopsies with a higher overall score showed aging-direction changes in genes outside the signature in all 11 cell groups (ρ = 0.37, permutation P = 0.008; Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_2">3c</ref>).
table.header: Spatial and expression changes in DKD
table.expanded: Within DKD, biopsies with a higher overall score showed aging-direction changes in genes outside the signature in all 11 cell groups (ρ = 0.37, permutation P = 0.008; Figure 3c).

table.formatted: After adjustment for age, sex, and baseline eGFR, patients with a higher overall tissue-aging score lost eGFR faster (partial ρ = -0.63; permutation P = 0.002; Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_3">4a</ref>,<ref type="figure">b</ref>).
table.header: Tissue-aging scores and eGFR decline in DKD
table.expanded: After adjustment for age, sex, and baseline eGFR, patients with a higher overall tissue-aging score lost eGFR faster (partial ρ = -0.63; permutation P = 0.002; Figure 4a,b).

table.header: Tissue-aging scores and eGFR decline in DKD
table.expanded: Results were similar in sensitivity analyses, and additional adjustment for proteinuria did not change the association (overall score, partial ρ = -0.61; permutation P = 0.0045).

table.formatted: In the 24 patients with an eGFR slope, higher PAS-estimated scores were associated with faster eGFR loss for all four compartments (partial ρ, -0.44 to -0.56; permutation P = 0.010-0.043), close to the associations of the transcriptomic scores (-0.58 to -0.69; Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_4">5c</ref>; Supplementary Table <ref type="table">S4</ref>).
table.header: Tissue-aging scores estimated from PAS histology
table.expanded: In the 24 patients with an eGFR slope, higher PAS-estimated scores were associated with faster eGFR loss for all four compartments (partial ρ, -0.44 to -0.56; permutation P = 0.010-0.043), close to the associations of the transcriptomic scores (-0.58 to -0.69; Figure 5c; Supplementary Table S4).

table.formatted: Genes with a DKD-versus-control false discovery rate below 0.05 were divided into those that changed with control age in the same direction (P < 0.05) and the remainder, and each set was tested for Hallmark and Reactome overrepresentation against the genes tested in that cell group.
table.expanded: Genes with a DKD-versus-control false discovery rate below 0.05 were divided into those that changed with control age in the same direction (P < 0.05) and the remainder, and each set was tested for Hallmark and Reactome overrepresentation against the genes tested in that cell group.

table.header: Spatial and cellular changes in control kidneys
table.expanded: The spatial aging index evaluated with each control excluded gave ρ = 0.613, a bootstrap 95% interval of 0.19-0.84, and age-permutation P = 0.022.

Spatial and expression changes in DKD compared with control aging. a: Sex-adjusted control-age effect against the age-and sex-adjusted DKD-versus-control effect for 66 cell-pair proximity measurements (ρ = 0.65; 80.3% of pairs in the same direction; permutation P = 0.0066); labeled pairs are shown in b. b: Control-age and DKD-versus-control effects with 95% confidence intervals for five anatomical pairs. c: Correlation between control-age effects and DKD-versus-control effects (left) or overall-score effects within DKD (right) across genes outside the signatures, by cell group and pooled.

table.formatted: Gray bars show the 2.5th-97.5th percentiles of 1,000 permutations; filled points, permutation P < 0.05. d: Hallmark pathways enriched among genes that differed between DKD and control tissue, separated into those that changed in the same direction with control age and those that did not.

report: Reporting *p* values imprecisely (e.g., *p* < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in *p* value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., *p* = .032) unless *p* values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use *p* < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., "decreased at the *p* < .05 significance threshold").

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"} The APA manual states: Report exact *p* values (e.g., *p* = .031) to two or three decimal places. However, report *p* values less than .001 as *p* < .001. However, 2 decimals is too imprecise for many use-cases (e.g., a *p* value meta-analysis), so report *p* values with three digits. American Psychological Association (2020). Publication manual of the American Psychological Association, 7 edition. American Psychological Association. :::
